title: Jefferson's Code No. 11 (the Barclay-Lamb code), coded passages of Barclay, Carmichael, Short and Jefferson, 1786-1791 (catalogue 483)

steps.what: Founders Online search 'Code No. 11': 18 documents 1786-1791; editors decoded from a partial reconstruction, no key found; no published key table found on the web or in cryptiana.
Founders text fetched through the built-in browser (WAF on plain HTTP); LoC item JSON gave master images on tile.loc.gov; 71 frames of 15 letters downloaded.
Two subagents transcribed the coded groups of TJ's copies (with clear sheets) and of Barclay's and Carmichael's letters with TJ's interlinear decodings.
Aligned the 40-group test line of TJ to Carmichael 15 Dec 1787 with the opening of his 14 Jun 1787 letter (PrC fetched); groups 14-40 fit; two misprints in the printed line found (519, 1097).
Segmentation solver (DP, then beam search keeping one value per repeated code) to cut each passage's plaintext among its groups; wrong seed values propagated; set aside.
attested_key.py: values only from TJ's interlinear decodings, clear-text sheets and printed pairs (key.tsv).

Checked each editors' conjecture against every occurrence of its groups: 1420 = de confirmed (De-ar Si-r); 1089 = -al (imperi-al); 495 = larg- in Barclay 1786 contradicts [sea]; 537 = u splits Kentuck[ians] differently; 1107 = t gives t-alk and Braban-t.

Barclay's undated ca. 3 Jul 1787 letter found filed under 12 Jun 1787 (007_0476-0481) by contact sheets of tile.loc.gov thumbnails; footnotes 1196.1084?.758.861.1307.626 and 265 (= Congress, confirmed).
TJ to Carmichael 11 Apr 1791 located by probing tile.loc.gov volumes (LoC item pages behind a bot check); 544 groups transcribed against the 'decyphered' sheet.
Short's despatches to Jay (NARA M34 roll 2, catalogue proxy): coded passages in Nos. 2, 5 and 6 (Oct 1789), the last not in the Founders hits; decodings in the State Department copy for Nos. 2 and 6.
make_reading.py: 1,868 of 1,917 counted groups carry a reading (97.4%), graded H/C/M/I.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1269 tokens, 509 types, en-modern order 4: reading -2.137 per letter; polyphonic: 25% of read tokens differ from their type's commonest value. Verdict: not applicable.

Read share recounted over cipher words only (README Conventions, 16 Nov 2026), holes by words, sure words only. The reading files hold the coded words alone (the letters' clear text is not in them), so nothing was split; the count is by hand because the files mark doubt with a bare ? and bracketed syllables, which v10_relabel.py does not read as holes (and the generator make_texts.py was not rerun). Moves: Carmichael 5 Jun 1788 1.0 -> 0.941, 24 Jul 1788 1.0 -> 0.920, 26 Jan 1789 1.0 -> 0.926, Jefferson 9 Aug 1789 1.0 -> 0.765 and Short 25 Oct 1789 1.0 -> 0.943 (group 1612, Marquis twice, no key value) go from read to read in part; read in part, figure changed: Barclay's footnotes 0.857 -> 0.500, Jefferson 4 Jul 1787 0.941 -> 0.556 (5 of 9 cipher words), 15 Dec 1787 0.775 -> 0.913, 25 Dec 1788 0.875 -> 0.706; still read: Barclay 10 Apr 1786 0.991, Jefferson 25 Sep 1787 0.993, Carmichael 8 May 1788 0.971 and 29 May 1788 0.957, Jefferson 3 Jun 1788 1.0, Short 9 Oct and 28 Oct 1789 1.0, Jefferson 11 Apr 1791 1.0. Grade M groups (216, the editors' reading with no second occurrence) are not marked in the files and are not counted as holes here.

Decrypt audit (research/decrypt_audit, 124 of 508 words flagged in 5 letters): the readings do not pass through key.tsv. Each group's reading is the plain column of transcription/*.tsv (Jefferson's interlinear or clear sheet, the clerk's decoding, or the editors' text), copied by make_reading.py and make_texts.py; reading.tsv and 16 of 18 reading files regenerate exactly from those tables. Of 1,904 groups with a reading, 807 have the value key.tsv gives, 727 are numbers not in key.tsv, 301 have another value there, 44 meet a note or mark standing as a value in key.tsv, 25 are punctuation. Found: 19 groups graded H (16 words) print the editors' word against Jefferson's decoding with no bracket; 13 more print Jefferson's own written correction; key.tsv carries notes and phrases as values for about 20 numbers (1420, 1166, 1390, 1252, 1399 and others). No file other than NOTES and this profile changed; audit figures unchanged.

Decrypt audit, repair round: each of the 18 texts/*_reading.txt given a header line saying it is Jefferson's decodings and sheets and the editors' text, not the output of key.tsv. The 19 groups that print the editors' word against Jefferson's decoding regraded H to M in six texts/*_decryption.txt files, with a header line in each; no word changed. reading.tsv, the grade counts in this profile (H 1,519, M 216) and the page were not recomputed (H 1,500, M 235 with the regrade). key.tsv not touched. Two page sentences on the key corrected.

validation.notes: polyphonic: 25% of read tokens differ from their type's commonest value

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The 348 values of key.tsv come from Jefferson's interlinear decodings of Barclay's and Carmichael's letters, his clear-text sheets for his own coded letters, and the decodings in the State Department copies of Short's despatches, all in the same correspondence; no key sheet survives.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cipher words only, hand count of the 17 reading files with words (16 Nov 2026): about 1,200 words (variant and syllable fragments joined), about 45 holes (doubtful ? marks, grade-I conjectures in brackets, the unread groups), so about 0.96 of the words of the readings. This is an estimate: fragments of words in the files make the word count approximate. The 1,868 of 1,917 counted groups (0.974) of reading.tsv are a count of groups, and the Adams postscript (about 30 groups, blotted) is outside both. Before: 0.974 (groups).

outcome.notes: Every coded passage already had a printed reading by the Jefferson Papers editors (prior solution, used for alignment); 216 groups rest only on it (grade M). The work adds the first value table of Code No. 11 and corrections: Barclay's footnote has six groups (The Pro-cur-e-r [General?]), [sea] at 495 is contradicted (495 = larg-), Kentuck[ians] splits as Ke-nt-u-[814], [tal]k is t-alk, and the printed 15 Dec 1787 test line has two misprints.

texts.label: Barclay to the American Commissioners, Madrid, 10 Apr 1786
texts.summary: Barclay reports from Madrid that Lamb's mission to Algiers has failed: no peace without a larger sum, and the Dey refuses to treat.

reading_review.note: The coded paragraph reads through as sentences (no peace without a larger sum; the Dey refuses to treat); Jefferson's interlinear decoding throughout.

texts.note: 16 Nov 2026, cipher words only, sure words only, counted by hand on the reading file (it holds the coded words alone; the clear text of the letter is not in it): about 111 words, 1 doubtful (think ?): 110 read; ? after a word or alone is a doubtful or unread group. Before 1.0 (counted over code groups). The tool v10_relabel.py does not read a bare ? as a hole and cannot be given a declaration for these files, so its figure differs.
